title: SignedPayload with a 65-byte payload encodes to a strkey the library's own parser refuses
severity_basis: Encode side only. stellar-xdr 28.0.0 and 28.0.1 pin stellar-strkey 0.0.13; stellar-strkey 0.0.17 (#107) enforces a 1 to 64 byte payload and stellar-xdr 30.0.0 pins stellar-strkey 1.0.0.

entries.expected: refuse to encode a signed payload of 65 bytes (SEP-23 and CAP-0040: 1 to 64 bytes)
entries.observed: Executed on 28.0.0 and 28.0.1, which pin stellar-strkey 0.0.13: SignedPayload with a 65-byte payload encodes to a 172-character P strkey, which the library's own parser refuses. stellar-xdr 30.0.0 refuses to encode it.

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --columns 'rust@*' --entries 'strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-65-bytes'), L4, on rust@28.0.0 and rust@28.0.1 (both profiles).
evidence.expected_basis: SEP-23 v1.4.0 and CAP-0040: a signed payload carries 1 to 64 bytes (opaque payload<64>), so its strkey is at most 165 characters.

reproduction.method: The upstream pull request states the 1 to 64 byte rule and adds it to the constructor; the kit's own run reproduced the pre-fix behaviour on 4 of 4 listed report rows, offline, and the fixed version refuses.

evidence_added.reason: Fixed upstream; the pull request enforces the 1 to 64 byte range on every SignedPayload, so no new evidence is added.

history.note: Created from the known divergences of strkey/api-encode-signed-payload-65-bytes that reference https://github.com/stellar/rs-stellar-strkey/pull/107 and their failure rows.
The upstream item already records this defect.
